# Modules

A module is a capability with its own files, dependencies and services, declared in
`modules/<name>/module.toml`. Nothing in a manifest registers a route, model, task or nav
entry — runtime conventions already do that, so composing a project is adding or removing
files. Only infrastructure needs rendering.

| Module | State | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| admin | installed | User management and a DB-backed permission system, behind an isolated /admin panel |
| ai | installed | Multi-provider LLM calls (LiteLLM) |
| analytics | installed | In-process SQL over Postgres (DuckDB) |
| auth | installed | Email/password login and session verification (bcrypt + JWT, no sidecar service) |
| cache | installed | Key/value cache (Valkey) |
| email | installed | Send email (SMTP, console backend for local dev) |
| jobs | installed | Durable background jobs (Temporal) |
| rag | installed | Embeddings + pgvector similarity search (RAG building blocks) |
| realtime | installed | WebSocket pub/sub (in-process locally, Valkey fanout across workers) |
| storage | installed | File storage / uploads (local disk, S3-compatible in production) |

Render a project without a module:

```bash
genesis render --out ../my-app --without jobs
```
